scope: Newest complete eligible machine cycle not previously processed by Beta. T0 backpressure active; no ordinary expansion. Independent structural review limited to TER and SERV, the live research items with current exact underwriting gates.
summary: No new structural blocker emerged. TER remains structurally exposed to AI test/advanced-packaging intensity with robotics as a secondary diversification path whose semiconductor/electronics correlation limits resilience. SERV addresses a genuine last-mile substitution opportunity, but economic capture still depends on utilization, autonomy reliability, partner access and financing surviving simultaneously. Current open defects are underwriting evidence defects, not structural-causal defects.

claims: The strongest causal chain remains AI/HBM/advanced-package complexity -> higher production-test and known-good-device value -> Teradyne test demand.
Robotics provides a labor/productivity pathway but is not a fully independent hedge because electronics/semiconductor customers are material to Robotics demand.
The current 2026 SBC/debt/repurchase normalization gap can change survival/dilution/capital-allocation treatment but does not invalidate the established structural bottleneck mapping.
causalEdges: AI/HBM complexity -> advanced packaging/test intensity -> Teradyne test demand
advanced-package yield cost -> known-good-device screening value -> Teradyne/TEL test-cell relevance
manufacturing labor pressure -> cobot/AMR adoption -> Robotics demand
falsifiers: Critical AI-device test shifts materially to substitute/captive architectures that reduce Teradyne content per device.
AI/semiconductor capex contracts while Robotics remains too correlated with electronics demand to diversify the shock.
Robotics fails to establish durable profitability or independent end-market demand.
risks: Customer concentration and semiconductor capital-cycle sensitivity remain structural counterweights.
AI centrality creates common-factor exposure as well as upside.
unknowns: Durability of test intensity per AI device across architecture transitions.
Long-run Robotics margin resilience and independence from semiconductor/electronics capex.

claims: The causal opportunity remains short-distance delivery labor/cost -> autonomous sidewalk substitution -> potential lower delivery cost where density and operating permissions support utilization.
Merchant/category/platform breadth can improve route density and utilization, but announcements alone do not establish economic capture.
The current cash-flow/equity-overhang/concentration gap is upstream survival evidence; it does not erase the structural use case but can prevent Serve from surviving long enough to capture it.
causalEdges: last-mile labor/cost -> sidewalk autonomy substitution -> Serve demand
partner/category breadth -> route density/utilization -> fleet economics
falsifiers: Utilization cannot absorb fleet, remote-operations and maintenance costs.
Platform access or municipal permissions narrow materially.
Human intervention intensity remains incompatible with attractive unit economics.
Expansion announcements fail to convert into recurring paid delivery volume.
risks: Capital intensity and financing can interrupt the causal path before scale economics emerge.
Partner breadth does not yet prove bargaining-power or revenue-concentration resilience.
unknowns: Paid-delivery density and contribution margin in mature markets.
Remote-assistance and maintenance economics at current fleet scale.
